summary: Phase 2 - Option A (Offline Mode) end-to-end testing. Service Worker registers (HTTP 200, controller live), OnlineStatusIndicator transitions En línea ↔ Sin conexión via Playwright context.set_offline(), checkout while offline enqueues the order in IndexedDB ('pos-offline'/pending-orders), pending counter shows '1 pendiente', and on reconnection the queue auto-syncs to /api/orders (IDB pending→0, order visible in /orders /api/orders persisted). Backend POST /api/orders curl regression passed.

ui_bugs.issue: After successful auto-sync the badge still displayed '1 pendiente' even though IndexedDB pending=0 and the order was actually persisted on the backend. Two indicator instances are mounted (sidebar + mobile floating wrapper) and the module-level `syncing` flag in offlineSync.js causes the second instance to early-return `{skipped:true}` and refresh `pending` BEFORE the first instance finishes, so the stale value sticks. Workaround: dispatch a `pos-queue-updated` event from offlineSync at the end of syncPendingOrders() (or after each removePendingOrder), so all mounted indicators refresh.

Success toast '1 orden(es) sincronizada(s)' was not detected by Playwright after 8s. Sonner toasts auto-dismiss in ~4s and only the indicator that actually performed the sync calls toast.success — the other instance gets `skipped:true` and shows no toast. Real sync did succeed (IDB cleared + backend has the order). Recommend extending toast duration to ~6-8s or moving the success toast outside the runSync race.

action_items: Fix stale 'X pendiente' badge after auto-sync: dispatch window event 'pos-queue-updated' inside syncPendingOrders (after each removePendingOrder OR at the end) so every mounted OnlineStatusIndicator re-reads pendingCount().
Consider raising toast.success duration for 'sincronizada' to ~6s, or call the success toast outside the syncing guard so it always fires once even when multiple indicators are mounted.

Persisted reset: cashier 'saiko' PIN was reset to 1234 via PUT /api/cashiers/{id} during this test (it had drifted again). Consider seeding/migrating PIN=1234 idempotently on app start so the demo flow keeps working.
critical_code_review_comments: offlineSync.js uses a module-scoped `syncing` boolean which serializes sync calls but causes the second OnlineStatusIndicator to silently skip and over-write its pending state with stale data — should broadcast a 'pos-queue-updated' event after the run.
POSPage.handleCheckout correctly branches on navigator.onLine AND falls back to enqueueOrder() on a network error post-online-check — defensive and correct.

sw.js correctly avoids caching /api/* and POSTs, network-first for navigation, cache-first for static assets — sound design. SHELL list however does NOT precache the hashed JS/CSS bundles (built into /static/js/main.*.js); the first load opportunistically caches them via the fetch handler, but a true cold-offline boot may fail until those bundles are visited once online.
offlineQueue.js uses keyPath 'localId' on object store; enqueueOrder generates a sufficiently unique localId. Good.
Backend POST /api/orders payload accepted with the offline-flushed body (verified via curl + via flushed-on-reconnect path).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (offline enqueue, online auto-sync, backend persistence all green; minor stale-badge + missed success-toast race noted)

rca of the issue: Stale '1 pendiente' badge after sync: two OnlineStatusIndicator React instances are mounted (AppLayout sidebar + mobile floating wrapper). Both fire runSync on the 'online' window event. offlineSync.syncPendingOrders has a module-level `syncing` guard that makes the second concurrent call early-return {skipped:true,synced:0,failed:0}. The second instance's `finally → refreshPending()` reads IDB BEFORE the first instance finishes removing items, so the stale `pending=1` is committed to the second instance's React state and never refreshed (no event is dispatched at the end of the real sync). Fix: dispatch `window.dispatchEvent(new Event('pos-queue-updated'))` inside syncPendingOrders after each `removePendingOrder` (or once at the end). This will trigger refreshPending in every mounted indicator.
